comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Fixed, but the symptom did not reproduce in the running app, and that
is worth recording rather than quietly inheriting. `ghostty_init` calls
Ghostty's `ensureLocale`, which derives a locale from CFLocale and
setenvs LANG and LANGUAGE across the whole process before Muster starts
its daemon - measured on a bundle opened under `env -i`. So a Dock
launch was already being rescued, by the renderer, one initialisation
step earlier.

That is an invisible loan on renderer init order: nothing states it, no
test holds it, and a libghostty that stopped calling `ensureLocale` - or
a Muster that started its daemon before `ghostty_init` - would break
panes with no edit to blame. Muster now decides its own daemon's
locale, so the loan is repaid rather than the break repaired.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`daemon::carried` allowlists `LANG`, the `LC_*` family and `TERM`, and a
window launched from a terminal gets all of them. A window launched the
way Muster is meant to be launched - Dock, Finder, Spotlight - gets none:
launchd hands a GUI process `HOME`, `PATH`, `SHELL`, `USER`, `LOGNAME`,
`TMPDIR`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` and little else. Measured on this machine with
a throwaway bundle opened under `env -i`, which is the closest thing to a
double-click a script can arrange.

So the allowlist carries nothing for them, the daemon runs in the C
locale, and every pane inherits it. That is exactly the failure the
allowlist's own comment says `LANG` is on the list to prevent: "a pane
mangles non-ASCII". `PATH` is the bare `/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`
for the same reason, which matters less - a login shell rebuilds it from
rc files, which is the whole argument for the list being short.

An allowlist can only carry what exists, so the fix is to supply what
launchd did not. Ghostty derives `LANG` from the macOS locale for this
reason, and its implementation is the reference. Questions worth
answering rather than assuming:

- Is this the shell's or the core's? Deriving a POSIX locale name from
  `CFLocale` is an OS question and belongs in the shell; deciding that a
  daemon with no `LANG` gets one is the core's. Probably: the shell
  reports what the platform says, the core decides whether to carry it.
- `TERM` has a different answer. herdr sets it per pane, and the value
  the daemon holds only matters for a process it starts outside one - so
  the honest fix may be no fix, and a note saying why.
- What does a run say it did? `daemon.environment` names carried and
  dropped variables; a supplied one is neither, and should read as
  supplied.

Found while diagnosing a window whose panes ran `/bin/sh`, which turned
out to be an unrelated scratch config. `SHELL` itself is fine - launchd
does supply it, so a Dock launch gets the user's real shell.
title: 🌐 A Dock-launched Muster has no locale and no TERM
